title: Crime Detection and Investigation
description: Study module for Crime Detection and Investigation (20% of the Criminologist Licensure Examination), organized by the topics and competencies of the PRC Table of Specifications.
source: PRB of Criminology Res. No. 02 s. 2024, as amended by Res. No. 06 s. 2025
status: Written with AI assistance from the TOS competencies and the laws they name; for faculty review (content/tos/SOURCES.md).

chapters.title: Fundamentals of Criminal Investigation and Intelligence
chapters.introduction: Criminal investigation identifies the offender, locates him and gathers the evidence to prove his guilt. Intelligence supports it with timely, evaluated information. This chapter covers the tools and phases of investigation, surveillance and intelligence, and the rules on arrest, search and crime scene work.
chapters.content:
## Fundamentals of Criminal Investigation and Intelligence

### 1.1 Objectives, tools and phases of investigation

TOS competency 1.1 (5 items): Explain the objectives of criminal investigation and principles of intelligence, tools of investigation, the cardinal points of investigation and phases of criminal investigation.

- Instrumentation is the use of scientific instruments and forensic methods.
- The phases: identify the offender, trace and locate him, then gather evidence to prove guilt.
- Principles of intelligence include timeliness, usefulness, security and continuity; late intelligence is useless.
- A confession still needs evidence of the corpus delicti (Rule 133, Sec. 3).

### 1.2 Surveillance, the intelligence cycle and informants

TOS competency 1.2 (5 items): Distinguish the procedures and principles in the conduct of surveillance, the intelligence cycle, informants and informer, distinction and classification information and documents.

- A stakeout is fixed surveillance; tailing is moving surveillance; roping is undercover work.
- A-1 means a completely reliable source and information confirmed by other sources.
- An informant gives information freely, often once; an informer gives it regularly, usually for a fee.
- Classification: Top Secret (exceptionally grave damage), Secret (grave damage), Confidential (damage), Restricted (official use only).

### 1.3 Arrest, search and crime scene methods

TOS competency 1.3 (5 items): Assess the kinds, principles, and procedures involving arrest including essential provisions of R.A. 7438 and R.A. 9745, search and seizure, methods of crime search and sketches.

- Search methods: strip or line, grid, zone or quadrant, spiral, and wheel.
- Sketches: rough sketch at the scene, then finished sketch; floor plan, locality, perspective and cross-projection sketches.
- A private person may arrest an offender caught in the act and must deliver him to the nearest police station without delay (Rule 113, Secs. 5 and 9).
- R.A. 7438 protects persons under custodial investigation; R.A. 9745, Sec. 8 excludes statements obtained through torture.

keyPoints.title: Objectives, tools and phases of investigation
keyPoints.note: Investigation aims to identify, locate and prove the guilt of the offender, using information, interrogation and instrumentation, and answering what, where, when, how, who and why.

keyPoints.title: Surveillance, the intelligence cycle and informants
keyPoints.note: The intelligence cycle runs from planning and direction to collection, processing, and dissemination and use; sources are rated A to F and information 1 to 6.

keyPoints.title: Arrest, search and crime scene methods
keyPoints.note: Use the strip method for large open areas, the zone method for buildings, and a cross-projection sketch to show marks on walls and floor together; confessions obtained by torture are inadmissible.

chapters.title: Specialized Crime Investigation 1 with Legal Medicine
chapters.introduction: Crimes against persons call for careful scene work and medical evidence. This chapter covers how each is investigated, the special laws on hazing and sexual harassment, and the legal medicine of death and wounds.
chapters.content:
## Specialized Crime Investigation 1 with Legal Medicine

### 2.1 Investigating crimes against persons

TOS competency 2.1 (5 items): Distinguish the different approaches in the conduct of criminal investigation for each crime falling under the crimes against person of the Revised Penal Code (murder, homicide, parricide, infanticide, abortion, physical Injuries, and rape), essential provisions of R.A. 8049 ‘Anti Hazing Law’ as amended by R.A. 11053, R.A. 7877 ‘Anti- Sexual Harassment Law’, R.A. 11313 ‘Safe Spaces Act’.

- Homicide and murder investigations focus on the cause of death, the weapon, and any qualifying circumstance.
- In parricide, the marriage or birth certificate proves the relationship.
- Under R.A. 11053, presence during hazing is prima facie evidence of participation as a principal.
- R.A. 7877 needs authority or moral ascendancy over the victim; R.A. 11313 also covers peers, public spaces and online harassment.

### 2.2 Death, post-mortem changes and wounds

TOS competency 2.2 (5 items): Examine the following: kinds of death and pathological classification of death and changes in the body after death, and classification and characteristics of wounds.

- Livor mortis settles in the lowest parts and becomes fixed after several hours; rigor mortis stiffens the muscles and then passes.
- Incised wounds are longer than deep, with clean edges; stab wounds are deeper than long; lacerated wounds have irregular, torn edges.
- Gunshot entrance wounds are usually smaller with inverted edges and a contusion collar; exit wounds are larger and everted.

keyPoints.title: Investigating crimes against persons
keyPoints.note: Save life first, then secure the scene; preserve the evidence of a rape victim (no bathing or changing clothes) and refer her to the Women and Children Protection Desk; prove the relationship in parricide.

keyPoints.title: Death, post-mortem changes and wounds
keyPoints.note: Somatic death is the stop of vital functions and molecular death follows hours later; lividity fixed in the wrong place shows the body was moved; tissue bridges point to blunt force.

chapters.title: Specialized Crime Investigation 2 with Interview and Interrogation
chapters.introduction: This chapter covers how investigators question witnesses and suspects within the law, and how crimes against property, carnapping, fencing, trafficking and money laundering are investigated.
chapters.content:
## Specialized Crime Investigation 2 with Interview and Interrogation

### 3.1 Interview, interrogation and statements

TOS competency 3.1 (5 items): Explain the kinds and methods of interview and interrogation, legal requirements for admission and confession, principles of dying declaration and independent relevant statement.

- Techniques include Mutt and Jeff, bluff on a split pair, the stern approach and extenuation; threats and torture are never allowed.
- A custodial confession must be in writing and signed with counsel (R.A. 7438, Sec. 2(d)).
- An independent relevant statement is admitted to prove that words were said, not that they were true.
- A dying declaration is an exception to the hearsay rule.

### 3.2 Crimes against property and special laws

TOS competency 3.2 (5 items): Distinguish the different approaches in the conduct of criminal investigation for each crime falling under crimes against property of the Revised Penal Code (theft, robbery, and estafa); essential provisions of R.A. 6539 ‘anti-carnapping law’ as amended by R.A. 10883, P.D. 1612 “Anti-Fencing”, Laws on Human Trafficking (R.A. 9208, R.A. 10364 & R.A.11862), stages of Money Laundering (RA 9160, RA 9194, RA 10167, RA 10365, RA 10927)

- An employee who keeps money received for the employer usually commits qualified theft, because he held it only materially.
- Estafa by misappropriation needs juridical possession, as by an agent or trustee.
- Recruiting workers and keeping their passports to force them to work is trafficking (R.A. 9208, as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862).
- The Anti-Money Laundering Council enforces R.A. 9160, as amended by R.A. 9194, 10167, 10365 and 10927.

keyPoints.title: Interview, interrogation and statements
keyPoints.note: An interview questions willing persons and an interrogation questions reluctant suspects; an admission acknowledges facts, a confession acknowledges guilt.

keyPoints.title: Crimes against property and special laws
keyPoints.note: Taking a motor vehicle is carnapping (R.A. 10883); possessing stolen goods is prima facie evidence of fencing (P.D. 1612); money laundering moves through placement, layering and integration.

chapters.title: Traffic Management and Accident Investigation with Driving
chapters.introduction: Traffic management keeps people and goods moving safely; accident investigation finds out what happened and who is at fault. This chapter covers the pillars of traffic management, the rules of the road and the main traffic laws.
chapters.content:
## Traffic Management and Accident Investigation with Driving

### 4.1 The pillars of traffic management and the agencies

TOS competency 4.1 (3 items): Explain the principles of the 5 components of traffic management and agencies involved.

- The LTO registers vehicles and licenses drivers; the LTFRB grants franchises to public utility vehicles; the MMDA, the PNP Highway Patrol Group and deputized LGU enforcers enforce traffic laws; the DPWH builds roads.
- Engineering covers road design, signs, signals and markings.
- Education teaches safe behavior; enforcement deters violations.

### 4.2 Registration, signs, signals and markings

TOS competency 4.2 (3 items): Discuss the purpose and functions of: registration and renewal (motor vehicles & driver's license), the various traffic signs, traffic light, pavement or road markings.

- Solid lines discourage or prohibit crossing; double solid lines prohibit overtaking.
- A yellow light warns that red is coming: stop if you safely can, otherwise proceed with caution.
- Vehicle registration and license renewal are handled by the LTO.

### 4.3 Driving, right of way and parking

TOS competency 4.3 (2 items): Use of the principles of driving, principles of right way, and rules governing parking.

- Yield to pedestrians on crosswalks and to emergency vehicles with sirens.
- Do not park within six meters of an intersection, in front of a private driveway or where signs prohibit it.
- Defensive driving: keep a safe distance, watch for hazards and adjust to conditions.

### 4.4 Drunk, drugged and distracted driving, and children on motorcycles

TOS competency 4.4 (3 items): Compare the various traffic violations under the following laws; Anti-Drunk driving (RA. 10586,) R.A. 10913, and R.A. 10666 in R.A. 11226..

- R.A. 10586: drivers in accidents causing death or serious injury undergo mandatory alcohol and drug tests.
- R.A. 10913 allows hands-free devices that do not block the driver's view.
- R.A. 10666: the child must reach the foot pegs, wrap his arms around the driver and wear a standard helmet, except in medical emergencies.

### 4.5 Accident investigation

TOS competency 4.5 (4 items): Evaluate the principles and procedures involving traffic accident investigation, classification of accidents, the principles of key events, different types of tire marks impression and other debris, last clear chance principle, state of necessity principle

- Accidents are classified as fatal, non-fatal injury or property damage only.
- Skid marks come from locked wheels; yaw marks from tires sliding sideways in a turn; both help estimate speed.
- Debris, gouges and final positions help place the point of impact.

keyPoints.title: The pillars of traffic management and the agencies
keyPoints.note: Traffic management rests on engineering, education, enforcement, environment and economy; fix a physical hazard with engineering, not tickets.

keyPoints.title: Registration, signs, signals and markings
keyPoints.note: Regulatory signs state rules, warning signs warn of hazards, and guide signs show routes; a broken white line may be crossed when safe.

keyPoints.title: Driving, right of way and parking
keyPoints.note: At an intersection without signals, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right (R.A. 4136, Sec. 42); parking on a crosswalk or within an intersection is prohibited (Sec. 47).

keyPoints.title: Drunk, drugged and distracted driving, and children on motorcycles
keyPoints.note: Texting while stopped at a red light still violates R.A. 10913; small children may not ride motorcycles on busy roads unless they meet R.A. 10666's conditions; suspected drunk drivers take field sobriety tests, then a breath analyzer.

keyPoints.title: Accident investigation
keyPoints.note: Key events run from perception to the point of no escape, maximum engagement and final position; the last clear chance doctrine makes liable the party who could last have avoided the accident.

chapters.title: Fire Protection and Arson Investigation
chapters.introduction: Fire investigators must understand how fire starts and spreads before they can tell an accident from arson. This chapter covers fire behavior, classes of fire and extinguishing, fire protection systems, the law on arson and the reading of fire scenes.
chapters.content:
## Fire Protection and Arson Investigation

### 5.1 Fire behavior

TOS competency 5.1 (4 items): Illustrate the concept of fire triangle and fire tetrahedron, product of combustion, types/sources of heat energy, methods of heat transfer, stages of fire development.

- Stages: incipient, growth, fully developed, and decay.
- Carbon monoxide is the deadliest product of combustion because it binds hemoglobin more readily than oxygen.
- Radiation can ignite a building across the street without contact.

### 5.2 Classes of fire and firefighting

TOS competency 5.2 (3 items): Apply the classification of fire, methods of extinguishing classes of fire, prevention, control and supression of fire, and phases of firefighting.

- Class K fires call for wet chemical agents; Class D for dry powder.
- Extinguishing methods: cooling, smothering, starving and breaking the chain reaction.
- Firefighting starts with size-up; overhaul searches for hidden fire afterward.

### 5.3 Detection, alarm and suppression systems

TOS competency 5.3 (2 items): Identify active and passive fire detection, alarm system, and suppression equipment.

- Heat detectors suit kitchens where smoke detectors give false alarms.
- Automatic sprinklers open when heat breaks the bulb or link.
- The Fire Code (R.A. 9514) sets requirements for buildings.

### 5.4 Arson under P.D. 1613

TOS competency 5.4 (3 items): Evaluate the acts which constitute the crime of arson under PD 1613.

- Special aggravating circumstances include spite or hatred, intent to gain, a syndicate, and concealing another crime.
- If the main purpose was to kill and fire was the means, the crime is murder; if the main purpose was to burn and someone died, it is arson (People v. Malngan).
- Destructive arson is punished under Art. 320 of the RPC, as amended by R.A. 7659.

### 5.5 The fire scene, origin and cause

TOS competency 5.5 (3 items): Evaluate the fire scene, fire origin and cause of fire, and burn patterns.

- Burn patterns must be read with other evidence, since ventilation can mislead.
- Investigators work from the least burned to the most burned areas.
- Cause is classified as accidental, natural, incendiary or undetermined.

keyPoints.title: Fire behavior
keyPoints.note: Fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen, plus an uninhibited chain reaction (the fire tetrahedron); heat spreads by conduction, convection and radiation; flashover marks a fully developed room fire.

keyPoints.title: Classes of fire and firefighting
keyPoints.note: Class A ordinary combustibles, B flammable liquids and gases, C energized electrical equipment, D combustible metals, K cooking oils; never use water on Class C.

keyPoints.title: Detection, alarm and suppression systems
keyPoints.note: Passive protection (fire-rated walls and doors) contains fire without activation; active protection (detectors, alarms, sprinklers) must sense and act.

keyPoints.title: Arson under P.D. 1613
keyPoints.note: Burning one's own property is arson when it endangers others; multiple points of origin and flammable substances not normally present are prima facie evidence of arson.

keyPoints.title: The fire scene, origin and cause
keyPoints.note: The bottom of a V-pattern and the area of deepest, lowest charring usually point to the origin; suspected accelerants are confirmed by laboratory tests of samples sealed in airtight metal cans.

chapters.title: Vice and Drug Education and Control
chapters.introduction: Vices and drugs are closely linked to crime. This chapter covers the nature and effects of alcoholism, prostitution and gambling, the commonly abused dangerous drugs, the chain of custody of seized drugs, and the main offenses under R.A. 9165.
chapters.content:
## Vice and Drug Education and Control

### 6.1 Vices and their effects

TOS competency 6.1 (3 items): Explain the nature and effects of vices (alcoholism, prostitution, gambling)

- Gambling laws: P.D. 1602 as amended by R.A. 9287.
- Trafficked persons receive protection and services under R.A. 9208, as amended.
- Prevention combines education, family support and enforcement.

### 6.2 Commonly abused dangerous drugs

TOS competency 6.2 (5 items): Differentiate the commonly abused dangerous drugs defined under RA 9165 (opium, morphine, heroin, cocaine, shabu, marijuana, and marijuana resin, ecstacy, inhalants), methods of administration, signs and symptoms of use, and effects.

- Cocaine and ecstasy are stimulants; inhalants are solvents sniffed from bags.
- Methods of use include smoking, sniffing, injection, swallowing and inhaling vapors.
- Naloxone reverses opioid overdose.

### 6.3 The chain of custody of seized drugs

TOS competency 6.3 (5 items): Examine the chain of custody requirement (confiscation and seizure of illegal drugs until destruction of confiscated item).

- The chain covers every recorded movement from seizure to court and destruction (DDB Reg. No. 1, s. 2002).
- Non-compliance does not void the seizure if justifiable grounds are proven and the integrity of the items is preserved; the prosecution must show earnest efforts to get the witnesses (People v. Lim).
- The inventory is done at the place of seizure, or the nearest police station if that is not practicable.

### 6.4 Offenses under R.A. 9165

TOS competency 6.4 (2 items): Identify various acts punishable under R.A. 9165 as amended (Illegal trafficking and possession).

- Use (Sec. 15) needs a positive confirmatory drug test.
- Other offenses: importation (Sec. 4), maintaining a drug den (Sec. 6), possessing paraphernalia (Sec. 12).
- Those convicted of drug trafficking cannot apply for probation (Sec. 24).

keyPoints.title: Vices and their effects
keyPoints.note: Alcoholism is a disease of lost control, dependence and withdrawal; jueteng collectors are punished by R.A. 9287; persons forced into prostitution are trafficking victims, not offenders.

keyPoints.title: Commonly abused dangerous drugs
keyPoints.note: Shabu is a stimulant (sleeplessness, dilated pupils, weight loss); heroin and morphine are opioids (pinpoint pupils, drowsiness); marijuana causes red eyes and increased appetite.

keyPoints.title: The chain of custody of seized drugs
keyPoints.note: The seizing officer marks the items at once before the accused; the inventory and photographs are made before the accused or counsel, an elected official, and the NPS or the media; the drugs reach the laboratory within 24 hours.

keyPoints.title: Offenses under R.A. 9165
keyPoints.note: Delivering drugs for payment is illegal sale (Sec. 5); having them without authority is illegal possession (Sec. 11).

chapters.title: Technical Writing 1 and 2 (Legal forms and Police Report writing)
chapters.introduction: Police work is recorded in writing. This chapter covers the affidavit and other legal forms, the police blotter and complaint sheet, investigation reports, and administrative issuances.
chapters.content:
## Technical Writing 1 and 2 (Legal forms and Police Report writing)

### 7.1 Affidavits, pleadings and the police blotter

TOS competency 7.1 (4 items): Classify the parts, types and purpose of an affidavit (Sworn Statement), pleadings (parts of a motion, manifestation, petition), and content of police blotter and complaint sheet.

- A manifestation informs the court of a fact without asking for relief; a petition starts a special proceeding.
- The blotter is the official daily record of incidents: entries are made promptly and never erased.
- Corrections are made by a single line through the error, with initials.

### 7.2 Police reports and the case folder

TOS competency 7.2 (4 items): Examine different police reports (case folder) and basic investigative report (spot, progress and final).

- Reports state facts accurately, briefly and objectively, without conclusions about guilt.
- The case folder holds the final report, affidavits, evidence documents and the complaint.
- An after-operations report covers a planned police operation.

### 7.3 Administrative orders and issuances

TOS competency 7.3 (2 items): Compare the different types of Administrative orders and issuances such as circular, memorandum order, special order.

- Good issuances state who must act, what to do, when and why.
- Travel orders authorize official travel.
- The right issuance makes its scope and authority clear.

keyPoints.title: Affidavits, pleadings and the police blotter
keyPoints.note: The facts a witness personally saw go in the body of the affidavit; the jurat certifies that the affiant swore before the officer; a motion asks the court for relief.

keyPoints.title: Police reports and the case folder
keyPoints.note: A spot report is the first report of an incident, usually within 24 hours; progress reports give developments; the final report sums up the whole investigation.

keyPoints.title: Administrative orders and issuances
keyPoints.note: A memorandum circular states a policy for all units until revoked; a special order covers specific personnel actions such as assignments.

chapters.title: Introduction to Cybercrime and Environmental Laws
chapters.introduction: Investigators now deal with crimes committed through computers and with harm to the environment. This chapter covers the main cybercrime and environmental laws, the cybercrime warrants and digital evidence, and how environmental cases are filed.
chapters.content:
## Introduction to Cybercrime and Environmental Laws

### 8.1 Cybercrime and environmental offenses

TOS competency 8.1 (3 items): Recognize the acts which constitutes as violation of RA 10173, R.A. 10175, Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998, RA 9147 (Wildlife Act), RA 9003 (Solid Waste Management Act), RA 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act) and, RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act)

- R.A. 10173 (Data Privacy Act) protects personal information.
- R.A. 9147 protects wildlife; R.A. 8749 is the Clean Air Act; R.A. 9275 is the Clean Water Act.
- The Fisheries Code is R.A. 8550, as amended by R.A. 10654.

### 8.2 Cybercrime warrants and digital evidence

TOS competency 8.2 (4 items): Use the Rules on Cybercrime Warrants, Basic Incident Response, and Procedure on seizing and collecting digital evidence and admissibility of digital evidence.

- Do not simply switch off a running computer: volatile data in memory would be lost.
- A matching hash value proves a forensic image is an exact copy (Rules on Electronic Evidence).
- Examinations are done on the copy, never the original.

### 8.3 Filing environmental cases

TOS competency 8.3 (3 items): Understand the Procedure in filing of Environmental Cases: (Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998, RA 9147 (Wildlife Act), RA 9003 (Solid Waste Management Act), RA 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act) and, RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act)

- The Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases are A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC.
- Remedies include the writ of kalikasan, continuing mandamus and environmental protection orders.
- Intergenerational responsibility comes from Oposa v. Factoran.

keyPoints.title: Cybercrime and environmental offenses
keyPoints.note: Accessing a computer system without right is illegal access (R.A. 10175); open burning of solid waste is prohibited (R.A. 9003); fishing with explosives is punished by the Fisheries Code.

keyPoints.title: Cybercrime warrants and digital evidence
keyPoints.note: A WDCD orders disclosure of data, a WICD allows interception, a WSSECD allows search and seizure, and a WECD is needed to examine data on a device already lawfully seized (A.M. No. 17-11-03-SC).

keyPoints.title: Filing environmental cases
keyPoints.note: Any offended party, peace officer or officer enforcing an environmental law may file a criminal complaint; any Filipino may file a citizen suit, even for future generations; a SLAPP may be raised as a defense.
